newsitem.title: UK: Four London shipbrokers set up derivatives group.
newsitem.headline: Four London shipbrokers set up derivatives group.

text.p: The four biggest London brokers of freight forward agreements (FFAs) have agreed to set up an association to tighten up the market in freight futures, one of the new group announced on Wednesday.
The new group is being set up by Cargill Investor Services Ltd, Clarkson Securities Ltd, GNI Ltd in association with Howe Robinson & Co Ltd and Simpson Spence & Young Futures Ltd, CIS said.
The aim of the FFA Brokers Association will be to create a set of standards to help develop freight derivatives in both the dry and wet cargo markets, CIS said.
There has been recent unease within the market following speculation about potential defaults on FFA payments.

CIS freight division manager John Banaszkiewicz said: "There is a need for joint action to help streamline market practices, standardise contracts and iron out new problems facing the market as they arise."
Other regulated intermediaries which are involved in the broking of FFAs and their promotion as over the counter principal-to principal contracts will be encouraged to join the association, he added.

Banaszkiewicz likened the move to developments in the general financial services market in the mid-1980s when brokers launched a dealers' association to promote professional standards. -Paul Berrill Reuters Shipping News + 44 171 542 4087. Fax 5017.
